source_citation: Brooks, T., Pope, D., & Marcolini, M. (1989). Airfoil Self-Noise [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5VW2C. Underlying experiments: NASA RP-1218 (1989).

features.name: attack-angle
features.note: UCI metadata labels Binary; file contains 27 distinct angle values from 0.0 to 22.2.

paper_overlap.note: Airfoil is absent from the official regression loader map and from the ten named paper datasets.

queries: repo grep under .RnD/source/ngboost for airfoil experiment paths
prior_application_search.finding: No NGBoost experiment path or dataset loader found in the pinned official repository. Prior targeted web/repo search (2026-08-23) found other models on airfoil noise tasks but no documented NGBoost application on this UCI table.
prior_application_search.limitation: Non-exhaustive. Absence from the selected paper and this bounded search does not prove global non-use.

condition_groups.definition: Unique tuple of (attack-angle, chord-length, free-stream-velocity, suction-side-displacement-thickness); frequency treated as within-condition sweep variable.
condition_groups.note: Each group is a frequency sweep at fixed aerodynamic settings; row-level splits can place different frequencies from the same condition in both train and test.

primary_row_level_paper_aligned.approach: Row-level random 90/10 train/test holdouts aligned with the official NGBoost regression script convention: 20 repetitions with np.random.seed(1); identical split draws reused across natural, ordinary, and homoscedastic variants.
primary_row_level_paper_aligned.validation_split: Optional inner 20% of the 90% train pool for stage selection only if mirroring the official script.
primary_row_level_paper_aligned.scientific_question: Probabilistic regression accuracy and ablation ordering under the same i.i.d.-row protocol used for Yacht/Kin8nm feasibility evidence.
primary_row_level_paper_aligned.leakage_risk: Moderate: frequency-spectrum points from the same wind-tunnel condition may appear in both train and test, optimistic for interpolation within a condition.

optional_grouped_robustness.approach: Hold out whole condition groups (e.g. 80/20 or 90/10 by group with fixed seed) so all frequency rows for a setting stay in one split.
optional_grouped_robustness.scientific_question: Generalization to unseen aerodynamic settings rather than unseen frequencies within seen settings.
optional_grouped_robustness.leakage_risk: Lower condition leakage; smaller effective test units (106 groups) and different target estimand than paper-aligned row split.
optional_grouped_robustness.status: Optional robustness check only; not frozen.

preprocessing_recommendation: Load tab-separated file without header; assign UCI variable names. Use raw numeric features directly for tree-based NGBoost (no mandatory scaling). Do not drop rows unless new evidence of corruption appears. Document any future target or feature transform explicitly in a pilot handoff.

feasibility.compute_estimate: Trivial on CPU for NGBoost at n=1503, p=5; comparable to or lighter than Yacht (n=308) per-feature work though more rows.
feasibility.ethics_privacy: Public NASA wind-tunnel experimental data; no personal identifiers; no special consent beyond standard research use and CC BY 4.0 attribution.

unresolved_concerns: UCI variable type for attack-angle says Binary but 27 distinct degree values observed in raw file (preserved discrepancy).
Primary row-level split aligns with NGBoost paper protocol but leaves condition-level frequency leakage; grouped robustness split changes estimand and has only 106 groups.
